paragraphs: We are a Baptist Christian community in the heart of Montevideo. For almost three decades we have gathered around the Word, the sacraments, and prayer. We are not a perfect church — and we do not pretend to be — but we do want to be an honest church, trying to live the gospel in ordinary life.

Our name comes from Hebrews 6:19: "we have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure." That image says a lot about us: ordinary people holding on to what sustains us when circumstances move.

blocks.text: We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure, entering the inner sanctuary behind the curtain.

sections.description: A church is not defined only by what it says it believes, but by what orders its life. These are the three convictions that shape almost everything we do in practice.

values.title: Family of faith

paragraphs: The history of Iglesia Bautista El Ancla has its roots in Misión Distrito Este, which began as an extension of the First Baptist Church, under the responsibility of pastor Juan Ramón Gómez. On December 23, 1945 the congregation adopted the name Iglesia Bautista Distrito Este and established itself as an independent church. In 1946 Juan Antonio Louise took the pastorate and, over the following years, different pastors led the congregation, generally for brief periods.

That changed with the arrival of Donato Ferranty in 1969, remembered as a significant figure in the history of the church. Unlike the previous pastorates, he remained at the head of the congregation for roughly twenty years, providing a stage of stability and continuity. Throughout that period membership held between 55 and 83 members, in addition to the people who regularly took part in the life of the church without being formal members.

His ministry was marked by a strong commitment to service, the study of the Bible and Christian formation. He also encouraged academic and theological preparation, urging those who had the opportunity to continue their studies at the seminary. That emphasis on formation drew many young people and students in particular, and helped shape an active community committed to the life of the church.

As part of the desire to extend the church's work to other places, during Ferranty's pastorate a property was acquired in the La Blanqueada neighbourhood, where a new mission began operating around 1984. It received the name “Misión El Ancla” (The Anchor), inspired by a large anchor found on the property at the time it was purchased. The kindergarten belonging to Iglesia Bautista Distrito Este was also moved to the new space, since the premises on Juan Ramón Gómez had become increasingly small for the many activities held there.

The early years of the property are also remembered through the congregation's oral memory: accounts from pastors and leaders of unusual experiences that took place there. Over time these testimonies were connected to stories about the use the property may have had before, and they remain part of the memories passed on by those who were present in those first years of Misión El Ancla.

In 1989 pastor Donato Ferranty passed away, closing a stage of great importance for the consolidation and growth of the church. The following year Ernesto Dianessi took the pastorate and carried forward the work developed over the previous decades. His ministry stood out especially for his service linked to JEBU, his care for young people and his commitment to family and community life. During his pastorate both Iglesia Bautista Distrito Este and the work at Misión El Ancla continued to grow stronger.

By 1991 the church had 61 members, alongside the work of Misión El Ancla, a Bible Club with around 30 participants and a discipleship program made up of another 10 people. For the context of Baptist churches at the time, these figures reflected an active community and a significant development across its different areas of work.

In this way, the work begun as Misión Distrito Este and strengthened over decades gave way to a new stage in the history of the community, closely tied to that property in La Blanqueada and to the name that would eventually identify it: El Ancla.
